segments.note: From Bakersfield the newly formed Southern Pacific pushed south and east into the Tehachapi Mountains, using roughly 3,000 Chinese laborers to build the famous Tehachapi Loop -- a 3/4-mile spiral that lets the track cross over itself to gain 77 feet of elevation, engineered by William Hood. Simultaneously, crews bored the 6,940-foot San Fernando Tunnel at the south end of the line (work began Mar 22 1875, holed through July 14 1876, first train Aug 12 1876), at the time the third-longest railway tunnel in the world.

segments.note: On September 5 1876, Southern Pacific president Charles Crocker drove a golden spike at Lang Station (near present-day Palmdale), joining the northward and southward construction crews and completing the very first rail connection between San Francisco and Los Angeles -- a quarter-century before the more direct Coast Line opened in 1901. Combined with the existing Sacramento-Oakland (western_pacific_1869.geojson), San Francisco-San Jose (sf_san_jose_railroad.geojson), and Sacramento-Fresno (cprr_sacramento_fresno.geojson) lines, this completed a continuous SF-LA rail route nearly 25 years before 1900. Frequency estimated, unsourced.

segments.note: Southern Pacific era; overnight service by the Owl (Oakland-Los Angeles) ran this route for decades. Even after the more direct, flatter Coast Line opened in 1901, San Francisco-Los Angeles trains kept using this San Joaquin Valley/Tehachapi routing as well, since it served the valley's own cities. Frequency estimated, unsourced.

segments.note: The streamlined San Joaquin Daylight (Oakland-Fresno-Bakersfield-Los Angeles via Tehachapi) launched July 4 1941, continuing the San Joaquin Flyer/San Joaquin name lineage dating to 1927; the Tehachapi Pass was its scenic highlight, though the slow grade was famously a drag on its schedule. It absorbed the Owl's patronage after that train was discontinued and made its last run April 30 1971, the day before Amtrak -- which did not continue it. The route survives today as freight-only UP trackage (the Tehachapi Loop remains one of the busiest single-track freight grades in the US, jointly used by UP and BNSF).
